links.outcome: F1 and compute cost of simple vs. complex NLP models for IBD cohort identification on the same data
links.effect: Fine-tuned DistilBERT F1 94.06%; BOW F1 93.38% at 1.63g CO2; LLMs F1 86.65% to 91.58% with higher compute cost (938.5 to 33884.4g CO2) and more bias.
links.quote: Older NLP approaches, such as BOW, can outperform modern LLMs in clinical cohort detection when properly trained.

unlisted_practices: Reporting environmental (CO2) cost of AI models
Releasing open-source models and weights for reproducibility

screen.reason: The study conducts a comparative benchmark of 15 NLP and LLM models on clinical cohort identification for inflammatory bowel disease from electronic health records, evaluating performance, compute cost/emissions, explainability, and bias.
